public_rationale: The measurable parts of the claim hold for late 2024. In OpenAI's own SimpleQA tests, no frontier model got 90% of the factual questions it chose to answer right, so each gave wrong answers to more than 10% of them. The paper also found that models consistently overstate their confidence, which fits a failure to sanity-check. Apple researchers found that one irrelevant clause in grade-school math problems cut accuracy by up to 65% in all frontier models, which fits 'boneheaded' reasoning and math errors. One caveat: these benchmarks are adversarial or perturbed, so they overstate error rates in everyday use. 'Superficial' cannot be measured. Still, 'frequently' and 'regularly' are moderate words, and the evidence meets them.
limitations: The benchmarks were built to be hard, so real-world rates may be lower.
No rates were attached to 'frequently' or 'regularly'.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI answers are often superficial, confabulate, fail to self-check, and regularly make basic reasoning and math errors.

statement.excerpt: GenAI answers are frequently superficial; they invent things (“hallucinations” or what I would prefer to call confabulations”), they fail to sanity check their own work, and they regularly make boneheaded errors in reasoning, mathematics and so on..

from_speaker: they fail to sanity check their own work
they regularly make boneheaded errors in reasoning, mathematics
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in normal use around January 2025, generative AI often gave fabricated answers, often failed to catch its own errors, and made simple reasoning and math mistakes often enough to matter.
'Frequently' and 'regularly' mean a meaningful, recurring rate, not most of the time.
'Superficial' is too vague to measure. I treat it as the overall summary and score the measurable parts: confabulation, self-checking, and reasoning or math errors.
He named no period. I use October 2024 to the post date (2025-01-13).
criteria.support_condition: Measurements from the period show that frontier models produce false facts at meaningful rates, are overconfident about wrong answers, and lose accuracy on simple reasoning or math under light changes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Measurements from the period show that frontier models rarely invent facts, reliably flag their own errors, and make few simple reasoning or math errors.
